promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 10 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Stick to three runs a week and keep the long run easy to build a solid base.

flags.title: Heart‑rate drift
flags.detail: keep HR under 150 on all runs. Volume increase: add only one more kilometre per week. Rest days: essential for recovery. Long run quality: maintain a steady easy pace. New runner status: avoid consecutive hard days.

answers.question: I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?
answers.answer: No, running every day would raise volume too quickly and could risk injury or burnout. Stick to the three planned runs and rest days.

new.analysis: The athlete has just started running, has only three sessions a week and is asking whether to add daily running to speed up progress.  Building a base for a 5‑k ten weeks out should be gradual, with most time in easy runs and a single longer effort each week.  Adding daily sessions would increase volume too quickly for a new runner and could raise injury risk or heart‑rate fatigue.  The plan keeps three runs: a moderate easy run on Monday, a slightly hillier easy run on Wednesday, and a longer easy run on Saturday, with rest days in between.  The long run stays in zone 2 with a target HR under 150 to maintain a low‑intensity base.  Flags focus on heart‑rate drift, volume growth, and the need to avoid overtraining.  No red flag symptoms were reported, so no safety callouts are needed.
